text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament sacked the executive director of Bulgaria's Foreign Aid Agency Emilia Maslarova and appointed Vladimir Abadzhiev as her successor.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet said in a declaration the country's progress towards democracy, stable relations with neighbouring Balkan countries and the NATO-Russia security pact gave grounds to expect early admission into the alliance.
-- Bulgaria's prime minister Ivan Kostov said that former interim finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski is most likely to head the Bulgarian National Bank under a currency board system.
-- Bulgaria will launch a 100-days programme to crack down on organised crime in the country, prime minister Ivan Kostov said at a meeting with the US ambassador in Sofia Avis Bohlen. @

-- A Bularian court in the northwestern city in Pleven is expected to rule on June 5 on an insolvency case against Bulgaria's second biggest Plama oil refinery filed by Bulgaria's First Private Bank over $10.6 million and 161.4 million levs of overdue debts, state news agency BTA said.
-- The International Monetary Fund extended its mission in Bulgaria to help reduce a large draft budget deficit a month before introduction of a restrictive monetary regime.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would raise its main interest rate to 48.72 percent annualy from 43.08 percent, effective from Monday.
-- Bulgaria plans to import 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat to cover a consumption gap and a further 50,000 tones of feed maize, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
-- Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy said it was ready to start an enlargement of a gas pipeline on Bulgaria's territory for transporting Russian gas to Turkey.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet said it would propose to parliament to sack Bulgaria's State Savings Bank (SSB) chairman Bistra Dimitrova and appoint Spas Dimitrov as her successor. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
